messages:
pd-incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-CC9A2 triggered for service=inference-router (queue_backlog). Severity=high. Alert: queue_depth > 40k for 10m; autoscaler desired_replicas=12 actual_replicas=4. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-CC9A2

maya (oncall): ACKing. On it. First pass: check queue depth, hpa status, recent scale events. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/queue-backlog. Tagging infra and eng-sre.

jon (eng-sre): I'm pulling metrics now. CloudWatch: queue_depth spike started ~11:03 UTC. Current queue_depth ~48,200. 95p latency for hosted API up from 120ms -> 3.2s. 5xx rate ~1.1% over last 5m. HPA shows desired=12 current=4, kube events show FailedScaling due to failed node provisioning.

infra-bot: AutoscalerEvent: ScaleAttempt {time: 2026-03-14T11:12:01Z, desired=12, actual=4, reason: InsufficientCapacity: could not provision nodes (spot capacity failure)}

maya (oncall): Ok — autoscaler can't get nodes. Trying manual emergency scale to reserved instance pool (if available) and then fallback routing. Trying manual scale to dedicated node pool named 'dedicated-inference' as temporary.

maya (oncall): Running manual ops:`
```
kubectl --context prod -n inference scale deployment inference-router --replicas=12
# then check pods
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep inference-router
```

jon (eng-sre): Manual scale command returned pending pods stuck in ContainerCreating. Node events show: `failed to schedule pod, no nodes available matching instanceType/gpu`. AWS logs: EC2 RunInstances failed with InsufficientInstanceCapacity.

rachel (platform): If we can't get more nodes in the region, we should flip routing to the warm-standby region (eu-west-1) for low-tier traffic and degrade batch processing for non-critical tenants. Propose update to routing policy: redirect 30% of traffic to inference-router-eu variant and reduce batching window to lower memory footprint.

maya (oncall): Agreed. I'll apply temporary route policy and open a support case with cloud provider to request capacity. Applying routing change now.

maya (oncall): Applying routing patch:`
```
# patch route config via control plane API
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://console.redwood/api/v1/routing/modify \
  -d '{"service":"inference-router","policy":"failover","rules":[{"percent":30,"region":"eu-west-1","model_variant":"fast-quant"}] }'
```

infra-bot: Routing change accepted by control-plane (txn id=tx-5582). New split: 30% -> eu-west-1. Autoscaler remains in degraded state.

sam (customer-ops): Customer impact summary: Hosted API error spikes reported by some customers. Top impacted orgs (by 5xx volume): acme-inc, travelbot, learnify. Not seeing major data loss but noticeable latency/regressions for interactive endpoints. CS notified acme-inc and travelbot with proactive message.

jon (eng-sre): Short-term mitigations in place: 1) routing split 30% to eu-west-1, 2) reduce batch window on high-latency routes (reduces memory per pod), 3) manual scale attempted. Next: try provisioning on-demand instances in a different AZ or use Dedicated pool failover.

maya (oncall): Attempting on-demand: raising nodegroup to use on-demand g5 instances in us-east-1a. If infra approves, we can spin up ~8 nodes and recover capacity faster than waiting for spot.

infra-bot: Request to cloud support submitted (case CS-44219). Suggestion from provider: try different instance family or launch in additional AZ (us-east-1b).

jon (eng-sre): While infra works the capacity case, I pushed a temporary HPA override to reduce target CPU threshold so HPA tries to request fewer, more performant pods (partial mitigation). Applied HPA patch: `kubectl patch hpa inference-router -p '{"spec":{"targetCPUUtilizationPercentage":70}}'`.

maya (oncall): Noted. Monitoring. Queue trending down slowly: 48.2k -> 36.8k after routing split and HPA tweak. Still above runbook critical threshold (10k).

rachel (platform): Also enabling model-variant fallback for small requests: prefer smaller quantized models for non-critical endpoints. Can someone update the model catalog routing flag?

jon (eng-sre): Doing that now. Patch to model catalog: `PUT /api/models/route?variant=quant-small&condition=payload_size<512` — applied. Expect CPU per-token drop ~20-30%.

sam (customer-ops): CS update: acme-inc reported degraded UX but not outage. They accepted the mitigation plan and asked for ETA. I gave an initial estimate: recovery likely within 30-60m pending node provisioning.

maya (oncall): PD: I'm going to escalate to second-level oncall and infra owner if we don't see steady improvement in 15m. For now I'm leaving the alert acknowledged. If queue <10k and 5xx <0.2% for two consecutive 5m windows, we'll resolve.

pd-incident-bot: Acknowledgement recorded by maya (oncall). Escalation timer set: 15m -> next level (infra-primary). If no progress, PD will auto-escalate.

jon (eng-sre): Quick health check commands I ran:`
```
# queue depth summary (promql)
sum(rate(inference_queue_length[1m])) by (shard)
# pods
kubectl -n inference describe pods inference-router-xxxxx | grep -A5 Events
```

maya (oncall): Update 11:40 UTC: queue 22.1k. 5xx down to 0.6%. Manual on-demand nodegroup creation in progress (infra). Keep watch on eu-west traffic — confirm no routing loops.

infra-bot: Nodegroup 'on-demand-inference-1' provisioning started (request id ng-9921). Expected time ~10-12m.

rachel (platform): I'll own the postmortem if we clear. Note: config-level mitigation (routing splits + quantized fallback) looked effective. We'll need to refine autoscaler fallbacks for spot failures.

maya (oncall): Handing off to rachel for next 2h window. Action items for next oncall:
- Keep manual scale until on-demand nodes come up and pods reach desired=12
- Watch queue target <10k and 5xx <0.2%
- Coordinate with infra to confirm nodegroup stability and AZ spread
- Draft customer-facing timeline for impacted orgs

rachel (platform): Taking over. I'll keep PD acknowledged and post updates here every 10m. Thanks maya.

pd-incident-bot: Incident note: acknowledged by maya, reassigned to rachel at 2026-03-14T11:44:50Z. If no further action within 15m, PD will escalate to infra-primary.

maya (oncall): leaving final debug snippet here in case it's useful later:`
```
# find pods stuck on ImagePullBackOff or scheduling errors
kubectl -n inference get pods --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide
kubectl -n inference describe pod inference-router-abcde | sed -n '1,120p'
```

rachel (platform): Quick update 11:52 UTC: on-demand nodes are up, pods scheduling. Current queue 6.4k. 5xx 0.18%. Rolling back temporary routing split to 10% now to normalize cross-region costs.

sam (customer-ops): Sending final customer note: Short incident caused latency and error spike for some customers; measures taken (routing split, quantized fallback, on-demand capacity) and services now recovering. Will follow up with full incident timeline.

rachel (platform): Closing criteria met. I'll keep this thread for the PM/pm follow-up and start rough timeline for postmortem. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
